STEP 1 - Scene: Two slices of thin-crust pizza (cheese, sausage/meat crumbles, red onion, green jalapeño or bell pepper rings) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly overhead. The plate is the meal; nothing else on it.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate roughly 26 cm across (the plate spans most of the frame, and the pizza slices are about 9-10 cm long, consistent with a plate of that size). Plate area ≈ 26 x 26 ≈ 676 cm² (square plate, using side length as the ruler).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Pizza slice 1: cheese, tomato sauce, sausage crumbles, red onion, green pepper/jalapeño rings
- Pizza slice 2: cheese, tomato sauce, sausage crumbles, green jalapeño rings

STEP 4 - Area: Slice 1 about 9 x 7 cm ≈ 60 cm² (~9% of plate). Slice 2 about 9 x 8 cm ≈ 65 cm² (~10%). Food covers about 19% of the plate; the two items split as roughly 9% and 10%, summing to ~19%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pizza is thin, about 1.2 cm thick including toppings.
- Slice 1: 60 cm² x 1.0 cm ≈ 60 ml
- Slice 2: 65 cm² x 1.0 cm ≈ 65 ml

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like slices/cheese-topped items at ~0.9 g/ml. Pizza is less dense than a solid slab, so the density reduction is already captured by the bulk factor.
- Slice 1: 60 ml x 0.9 ≈ 54 g
- Slice 2: 65 ml x 0.9 ≈ 59 g
Total ≈ 113 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked pizza (cheese, sausage, crust) is roughly 260-280 kcal/100 g; I use 270 kcal/100 g for the whole slices.
- Slice 1: 54 g x 2.7 ≈ 146 kcal
- Slice 2: 59 g x 2.7 ≈ 159 kcal
Total ≈ 305 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two thin pizza slices of roughly 55-60 g each is plausible (a typical thin-crust slice is around 80-110 g, so these are on the small side, consistent with the partial slices visible). Around 113 g and ~300 kcal for what is shown is reasonable; the estimate could be somewhat low if the slices are thicker than assumed.
